pr_title: Enable `Scrolling` signal when scrolling with middle mouse on `RichTextLabel` or `ScrollContainer`
pr_body:
Fixes #46421

Added new function to `ScrollBar` so that the bar could be scrolled in a way that would emit a `scrolling` signal. Edited  `RichTextLabel` and `ScrollContainer` to use such functionality so scrolling either using the mouse scrollwheel would cause the signal to be emitted from the `ScrollBar`
pr_comments:
Amended PR. Added `scroll_to` and made it so `scrolling` signal is only emitted if `scroll` or `scroll_to` function is called. Updated various function calls to use these functions so that signal continues to be emitted by their actions.

I feel this is more clear and consistent behaviour.
The scroll signal is not emitted when dragging.
ScrollContainer has some `set_value()`s from touch events that are not changed to the new method. Is this intended?

> ScrollContainer has some `set_value()`s from touch events that are not changed to the new method. Is this intended?

Guess I was unsure about touch events, since they kinda do a bit of momentum and physics rather than direct physical interaction, but I suppose it's best to change them.

There seems to be another bug. When you scroll continuously using mouse wheel, the signal will be emitted even if no scrolling happens. EDIT: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90988#discussion_r1575253338

> There seems to be another bug. When you scroll continuously using mouse wheel, the signal will be emitted even if no scrolling happens. EDIT: [#90988 (comment)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90988#discussion_r1575253338)

Fixed.

issue_context.title: Scrolling signal on RichTextLabel/ScrollContainer's scrollbar doesn't work when scrolling with scroll wheel
issue_context.body:
___

***Bugsquad note:** This issue has been confirmed several times already. No need to confirm it further.*

___

<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
-->

**Godot version:**
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->
3.2.4-rc3 (This is also an issue on 3.2.3).

**OS/device including version:**
<!-- Specify GPU model, drivers, and the backend (GLES2, GLES3, Vulkan) if graphics-related. -->
Windows 10

**Issue description:**
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->
The `scrolling` signal on a RichTextLabel's scrollbar will not emit when it's scrolled with the scroll wheel. Clicking and dragging it still works.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Make RichTextLabel
2. Add enough text to trigger the scrollbar to appear
3. Connect scrollbar's `scrolling` signal
4. Scroll with scroll wheel

**Minimal reproduction project:**
<!-- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
[test.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6043821/test.zip)
comments:
Is that signal emitted when using the mouse wheel on a ScrollContainer?

Also, it's possible that this is caused by the RichTextLabel itself intercepting the mouse input (mouse wheel usage counts as a button press).
No, it's not emitted when using the mouse wheel on a ScrollContainer as well.
I can confirm this issue is present on 3.3.2 as well for me

Can confirm on 3.5.1 stable mono.
[edit]
"scroll_started" and "scroll_ended" signals of scroll container does not work at all, no matter which child is used (Control, Label, Rect, etc.). While "scrolling" signal of scrollbar only works when scroll handle is grabbed.

Can confirm this is still current as of Godot 4.0.2, with the behaviour mentioned above:
- Scrolling with keyboard buttons or mouse wheel **does not** trigger signals
- Grabbing the scroller and moving it **does** trigger signals

> "scroll_started" and "scroll_ended" signals of scroll container does not work at all, no matter which child is used (Control, Label, Rect, etc.). While "scrolling" signal of scrollbar only works when scroll handle is grabbed.

This is a separate bug, already reported in #22936

It occurred to me that fast fix would just be to have "scrolling" fired whenever "_value_changed" is called, but that might be too broad.
Could I have some more direction for when "scrolling" is meant to be fired? I assume if its scrolled with keyboard or mouse then it should be fired, but if it's moved programmatically it shouldn't? The documentation just says "Emitted when the scrollbar is being scrolled."

review_comments: You can change this to compare `get_value()` with `p_position` and do early return.
Done. Will be in next push.
MouseMotion does not call `scroll()` anywhere, which is what caused the regression I mentioned.
Yeah, it calls `set_as_ratio` instead. I'll look into how to handle this.
Added checks around where `set_as_ratio` was called and send signal if it's scrolling
`scroll_to_ratio()` is an idea, but I'm not sure it's called enough for that.
